title_ar: الخريطة كلها: من الصفر لمنصة داتا بالـAI
title_en: The whole roadmap: from zero to an AI-powered data platform
how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

storyboard_notes.text: Front-loaded orientation stack (DD-P00-1, DD-P00-2 before CH-03; about 8 min shorter without DD-P01): give it a visual roadmap spine, an A-01 zoom-out and progress cues so it reads as an overview, not a delay. Director and educator lenses review it.
Stacked dives (DD-P00-1 + DD-P00-2, 13.7 min with no narrator): end the stack with the return-to-trunk motif.

sentences.ar: في الشرح بتاعنا النهاردة احنا مش بس حنمسك منهج تقني مدته 24 اسبوع ونقراه
sentences.en: In today's explanation we won't just take a 24-week technical curriculum and read it.

sentences.ar: لأ احنا هناخد المنهج الدسم ده ونحوله لرحلة ممتعة جدا
sentences.en: No, we'll take this rich curriculum and turn it into a really fun journey.

sentences.ar: تخيلوا معايا اننا بنبني مشروع تجارة إلكترونية من الصفر حنسميه ShopFlow
sentences.en: Imagine with me that we're building an e-commerce project from scratch; we'll call it ShopFlow.

sentences.ar: حنمشي معايا خطوة بخطوة من اول ما يكون فكرة بسيطة لحد ما يتحول لمنصة بيانات ذكية بالكامل بتشتغل بالذكاء الاصطناعي
sentences.en: We'll go step by step, from when it's a simple idea until it becomes a fully smart, AI-powered data platform.

sentences.ar: الرحلة دي متقسمة لمحطات بتنقلنا من الصفر للاحتراف
sentences.en: This journey is divided into stations that take us from zero to pro.

sentences.ar: هنبدأ بيه رحلة الصفر الأساسيات والبرمجة
sentences.en: We'll start with the zero journey: basics and programming.

sentences.ar: وبعدين هندخل على لما الديتا تكبر قواعد البيانات
sentences.en: Then we'll move to 'when the data grows': databases.

sentences.ar: تالت محطة هتكون هندسة البيانات الضخمة
sentences.en: The third station will be big data engineering.

sentences.ar: وبعدها دمج الذكاء الاصطناعي
sentences.en: After that, integrating AI.

sentences.ar: وأخيرا هنختم بيه من التعلم لسوق العمل
sentences.en: And finally we'll close with: from learning to the job market.

sentences.ar: الموضوع يبان كبير بس متقلقوش احنا هناخدها واحدة واحدة بطريقة سليسة جدا
sentences.en: It looks big, but don't worry, we'll take it one step at a time, very smoothly.

sentences.ar: خلينا نبدأ بأول محطة معنا، رحلة الصفر، الأساسيات والبرمجة
sentences.en: Let's start with our first station: the zero journey, basics and programming.

sentences.ar: قبل ما نكتب أي كود معقد، لازم نفهم الأول الكمبيوتر ده بيفكر إزاي إزاي بياخد input ويخزنه في الميموري ويطلعه كـoutput
sentences.en: Before writing any complex code, we must first understand how the computer thinks: how it takes input, stores it in memory and returns it as output.

sentences.ar: المنهج ده بيعتمد على حاجة اسمها الفشل الأول أو Failure-first
sentences.en: This curriculum relies on something called failure first.

sentences.ar: بمعنى إيه؟ تخيلوا كده إن ShopFlow في أول أيامه كان مجرد Python script بسيط جدا
sentences.en: What does that mean? Imagine that in its first days ShopFlow was just a very simple Python script.

sentences.ar: وفجأة، البرنامج كله وقع وحصل runtime error بسبب bad file path أو مسار ملف غلط
sentences.en: Suddenly the whole program crashed with a runtime error because of a bad file path, a wrong file path.

sentences.ar: الموقف ده بيثبت لنا عملياً ليه تعامل مع الأخطاء أو الـerror handling مش مجرد رفاهية
sentences.en: This situation proves to us in practice why error handling is not just a luxury.

sentences.ar: ده أساس لازم نفهمه كويس قوي قبل ما نبني أي حاجة تانية
sentences.en: It's a foundation we must understand very well before building anything else.

sentences.ar: طيب عشان نعالج المشكلة دي ونوقف ShopFlow على رجليه من تاني الـ data بتمشي في مسار محدد
sentences.en: To fix this problem and get ShopFlow back on its feet, the data moves along a defined path.

sentences.ar: أول حاجة الـ raw data بتدخل وبعدين بتتعالج جوه الميموري تحديداً في الـ stack والـ heap وفي النهاية بتتحفظ في persisted file
sentences.en: First the raw data comes in, then it's processed in memory, specifically in the stack and the heap, and finally it's saved to a persisted file.

sentences.ar: في المرحلة دي الشغل كله بيكون مبني على الأساسيات زي الـ variables والـloops وطبعاً عمليات الـ CRUD
sentences.en: At this stage all the work is built on fundamentals like variables, loops and, of course, CRUD operations.

sentences.ar: وهنا بقى فيه نصيحة في منتهى الأهمية
sentences.en: And here's an extremely important tip.

sentences.ar: قبل ما نجري نسأل جوجل عن أي error يظهر لازم وبأكد لازم نقرأ terminal output الأول
sentences.en: Before we rush to ask Google about any error that appears, we must, I insist, read the terminal output first.

sentences.ar: صدقوني الإجابة دايماً بتكون مستخبية هناك
sentences.en: Believe me, the answer is always hidden there.

sentences.ar: خلينا ننقل على الخطوة اللي بعدها ونشوف الموضوع ده بيكبر إزاي
sentences.en: Let's move to the next step and see how this grows.

sentences.ar: القسم الثاني لما الديتا تكبر قواعد البيانات
sentences.en: Section two: when the data grows, databases.

sentences.ar: مع الوقت ShopFlow بيكبر وطلباته بتكتر
sentences.en: Over time ShopFlow grows and its orders multiply.

sentences.ar: هنا بقى الملفات البسيطة وجداول الـ spreadsheets بتبدأ تقع وتكون بطيئة جداً
sentences.en: Here the simple files and spreadsheet tables start to crash and become very slow.

sentences.ar: والمصيبة الأكبر إن الديتا نفسها ممكن تضيع
sentences.en: And the bigger disaster is that the data itself can get lost.

sentences.ar: عشان كده التطور المعماري الطبيعي هو عزل الشغل على SQL Database قوية زي Postgres أو MySQL
sentences.en: That's why the natural architectural evolution is moving the work onto a strong SQL database like Postgres or MySQL.

sentences.ar: وهنا إحنا مش بس بندور على مساحة تخزين إحنا بندور على الأمان اللي بتوفره خصائص ACID أو ACID Properties
sentences.en: And here we're not only looking for storage space; we're looking for the safety that ACID properties provide.

sentences.ar: ودي اللي بتضمن إن لو فيه أكتر من عملية بتتم في نفس اللحظة زي ما بنسميها Concurrent Transactions مفيش أي ديتا هتضيع أو تتكتب فوق التانية بالغلط أبداً
sentences.en: These guarantee that if several operations happen at the same moment, what we call concurrent transactions, no data is ever lost or overwritten by mistake.

sentences.ar: إزاي بقى بنربط الديتا ببعضها؟
sentences.en: So how do we connect data together?

sentences.ar: لو عايزين نربط جداول المستخدمين بطلباتهم في ShopFlow عندنا أدوات سحرية
sentences.en: If we want to join the users tables with their orders in ShopFlow, we have magic tools.

sentences.ar: وطبعاً مش هننسى الـ Window Functions اللي بتعتبر سحر حقيقي في الحسابات التراكمية
sentences.en: And of course we won't forget Window Functions, which are real magic for cumulative calculations.

sentences.ar: بصوا باع المثيرة للاهتمام هنا بجد هو السحر اللي بيعمله أمر EXPLAIN
sentences.en: Look, the really interesting part here is the magic the EXPLAIN command does.

sentences.ar: أحياناً بيكون عندنا query بطيئة جداً بشكل مستفز وده غالباً لأنها بتعمل full table scan
sentences.en: Sometimes we have an annoyingly slow query, and that's usually because it's doing a full table scan.

sentences.ar: أمر EXPLAIN بيفضح المشكلة دي فوراً
sentences.en: The EXPLAIN command exposes this problem immediately.

sentences.ar: النتيجة السرعة بتتضاعف بشكل خرافي والـquery اللي كانت بطيئة بتبقى طلقة
sentences.en: The result: speed multiplies incredibly, and the query that was slow becomes lightning fast.

sentences.ar: طيب وصلنا لمرحلة الوحش القسم الثالث هندسة البيانات الضخمة
sentences.en: OK, we've reached the beast stage: section three, big data engineering.

sentences.ar: النقلة دي هي التطور المعماري المطلوب عشان ShopFlow يتحول من مجرد مشروع عادي لمنصة عملاقة أو Enterprise Level Platform
sentences.en: This leap is the architectural evolution ShopFlow needs to turn from an ordinary project into a giant, enterprise-level platform.

sentences.ar: هنا بنواجه سيناريو فشل مرعب شوية
sentences.en: Here we face a rather scary failure scenario.

sentences.ar: إيه اللي هيحصل لو المنصة وصل عدد مستخدمينها لمليون مستخدم في اليوم وفجأة السيرفر الوحيد اللي شايل الشيلة دي كلها وقع
sentences.en: What happens if the platform reaches a million users a day and suddenly the single server carrying all that load crashes?

sentences.ar: إزاي هيتم التعامل مع الكارثة دي ومشاكل زي الـ Data Skew
sentences.en: How will this disaster be handled, along with problems like data skew?

sentences.ar: الموقف ده بيأكد إن الاعتماد على الأنظمة الموزعة أو Distributed Systems ما بقاش مجرد اختيار ده بقى ضرورة حتمية عشان النظام يفضل عايش
sentences.en: This situation confirms that relying on distributed systems is no longer just an option; it's an absolute necessity to keep the system alive.

sentences.ar: وعشان يتم إدارة الشغل المعقد ده من غير توهان بنحتاج اختصار عبقري اسمه DAG أو Directed Acyclic Graph
sentences.en: And to manage this complex work without getting lost, we need a brilliant abbreviation called DAG, or Directed Acyclic Graph.

sentences.ar: ببساطة كده ده هيكل تنظيمي بيخلي الـtasks تمشي في اتجاه واحد بس ومستحيل ترجع لورا وتعمل loop
sentences.en: Simply put, it's an organizing structure that makes tasks flow in one direction only, and they can never go back and form a loop.

sentences.ar: أدوات زي Apache Airflow بتنظم الـ Data Pipelines دي بمنتهى الكفاءة
sentences.en: Tools like Apache Airflow orchestrate these data pipelines very efficiently.

sentences.ar: والسر المعماري الحقيقي هنا هو مبدأ الـ Idempotency
sentences.en: And the real architectural secret here is the principle of idempotency.

sentences.ar: يعني لو حصلت أي مشكلة واضطرنا نعيد Task النظام بيضمن بنسبة 100% أن مستحيل Data ShopFlow تتكرر مرتين
sentences.en: Meaning if any problem happens and we have to rerun a task, the system guarantees 100% that ShopFlow data can never be duplicated.

sentences.ar: دي بقى المكونات الأساسية للـtech stack بتاع الـ Big Data
sentences.en: So these are the core components of the big data tech stack.

sentences.ar: الأساس بيبدأ بـ Apache Spark والحسابات الموزعة
sentences.en: The foundation starts with Apache Spark and distributed computing.

sentences.ar: وطبعاً Kafka عشان الـ Real Time Event Streaming
sentences.en: And of course Kafka for real-time event streaming.

sentences.ar: وبيجي معاهم HDFS عشان التخزين والـReplication
sentences.en: And alongside them HDFS for storage and replication.

sentences.ar: بس البطل الحقيقي والمميز هنا هو Apache CarbonData
sentences.en: But the real standout hero here is Apache CarbonData.

sentences.ar: ليه؟ لأنه بيقدم Analytical Queries أو استعلامات أسرع بمراحل من الصيغ العادية
sentences.en: Why? Because it delivers analytical queries much faster than ordinary formats.

sentences.ar: وده بفضل تقنية Multi-Level Indexing اللي بتوصل للديتا في أجزاء من الثانية
sentences.en: That's thanks to multi-level indexing, which reaches the data in fractions of a second.

sentences.ar: بعد ما بنينا الأساس القوي ده هندخل على القسم الرابع والطبقة المستقبل دمج الذكاء الاصطناعي
sentences.en: Having built this strong foundation, we move to section four, the future layer: integrating AI.

sentences.ar: إحنا هنا بنحول الـdashboards الثابتة والمملة لمساعد ذكي بياخد قرارات لوحده Autonomous Assistant
sentences.en: Here we turn static, boring dashboards into a smart assistant that makes decisions on its own, an autonomous assistant.

sentences.ar: بس قبل ما نغرق في المصطلحات التقنية المكلكعة خلينا نقف شوية قدام النصيحة الذهبية دي من المنهج
sentences.en: But before we drown in complicated technical terms, let's pause a moment at this golden tip from the curriculum.

sentences.ar: Don't memorize syntax, understand the data flow
sentences.en: Don't memorize syntax, understand the data flow.

sentences.ar: الهدف مش حفظ أكواد الأكواد دايما بتتغير
sentences.en: The goal isn't memorizing code; code always changes.

sentences.ar: لكن العقلية الهندسية الصح هي اللي بتفهم مسار الديتا وتدفقها
sentences.en: But the right engineering mindset is the one that understands the data's path and flow.

sentences.ar: دي العقلية اللي بتخلي أي مهندس يقدر يحل أي مشكلة تواجهه مهما كانت الأداة اللي بيستخدمها
sentences.en: That mindset lets any engineer solve any problem they face, whatever tool they use.

sentences.ar: من أهم التقنيات هنا هي الـ RAG أو Retrieval Augmented Generation
sentences.en: One of the most important techniques here is RAG, or Retrieval Augmented Generation.

sentences.ar: المفهوم ده حرفياً بيحل أكبر مشكلة في الذكاء الاصطناعي الهلوسة
sentences.en: This concept literally solves the biggest problem in AI: hallucination.

sentences.ar: بدل من سيب الـ AI يخمن ويألف إجابات غلط بيتم دمج Large Language Models مع قواعد البيانات الخاصة والمقفولة بتاعة ShopFlow
sentences.en: Instead of letting the AI guess and make up wrong answers, large language models are combined with ShopFlow's private, closed databases.

sentences.ar: بنستخدم حاجة اسمها Vector Embeddings عشان النظام يسحب معلومات حقيقية ودقيقة ويطلع إجابة مبنية على حقائق مش مجرد توقعات
sentences.en: We use something called vector embeddings so the system pulls real, accurate information and gives an answer built on facts, not just guesses.

sentences.ar: وهنا بتكمل الصورة مع الـReAct Agent Loop
sentences.en: And here the picture is completed with the ReAct agent loop.

sentences.ar: الـ AI هنا مش مجرد نموذج بيرد بكلام مكتوب وخلاص لأ ده بيفكر وبياخد أكشن حقيقي
sentences.en: The AI here isn't just a model that replies with written text; no, it thinks and takes real action.

sentences.ar: بيستلم الهدف بيختار الأداة المناسبة زي إنه ينفذ أمر SQL execution بنفسه وبعدين يجيب الـ data المطلوبة وفي الآخر يعمل generate للإجابة
sentences.en: It receives the goal, picks the right tool, like running an SQL command itself, then fetches the needed data, and finally generates the answer.

sentences.ar: ده تفاعل حقيقي بيخلي الذكاء الاصطناعي جزء شغال بجد وفعال جوه النظام
sentences.en: That's real interaction that makes AI a genuinely working, effective part of the system.

sentences.ar: طيب النقطة الحاسمة بقى هنا القسم الخامس من التعلم لسوق العمل
sentences.en: OK, now the decisive point: section five, from learning to the job market.

sentences.ar: إزاي ممكن نحول كمية المعرفة دي كلها لمهارات جاهزة ومطلوبة في سوق العمل
sentences.en: How can we turn all this knowledge into ready, in-demand skills for the job market?

sentences.ar: المنهج متقسم بذكاء على 24 أسبوع كمسار زمني واضح
sentences.en: The curriculum is smartly split over 24 weeks as a clear timeline.

sentences.ar: البداية بتكون بإتقان الـSQL في أول 4 أسابيع
sentences.en: It starts with mastering SQL in the first 4 weeks.

sentences.ar: وبعدين بناء أساسيات Python من الأسبوع 8 لـ11
sentences.en: Then building Python basics from week 8 to 11.

sentences.ar: ولما نوصل للأسبوع 18 بندخل في الـDAG وAirflow
sentences.en: When we reach week 18, we get into DAGs and Airflow.

sentences.ar: لحد ما نختم في الأسابيع من 21 لـ 24 بدمج الـ AI والـ Autonomous Agents
sentences.en: Until we finish in weeks 21 to 24 by integrating AI and autonomous agents.

sentences.ar: خريطة الطريق متكملة بتمشي خطوة بخطوة على أرض صلبة
sentences.en: The roadmap is complete, moving step by step on solid ground.

sentences.ar: وفي الرحلة زي الممارسة العملية هي كل حاجة
sentences.en: And on the journey, hands-on practice is everything.

sentences.ar: المطلوب هنا هو الخروج بـ Artifacts حقيقية ورفعها على GitHub
sentences.en: What's required here is to come out with real artifacts and push them to GitHub.

sentences.ar: يعني إيه؟ يعني تقارير مبنية على Tuned SQL Queries وAPIs محمية مكتوبة بـ Python أو Java
sentences.en: What does that mean? Reports built on tuned SQL queries, and secured APIs written in Python or Java,

sentences.ar: وتطبيقات Dockerized معها CI/CD زائد Airflow Pipelines شغالة Automatic ونماذج حية وشغالة للـ AI agents
sentences.en: Dockerized apps with CI/CD, plus Airflow pipelines running automatically, and live working models for AI agents.

sentences.ar: الحاجات دي هي الدليل العملي اللي بيثبت لأي شركة القدرة التامة على التعامل مع أنظمة الإنتاج وتحدياتها المعقدة
sentences.en: These things are the practical proof that shows any company your full ability to handle production systems and their complex challenges.

sentences.ar: الرقم 3 الرقم ده مش مجرد رقم ده المعيار الذهبي عشان أي حد يقدر يلفت انتباه الريكروترز ويتميز بجد في أي مقابلة عمل
sentences.en: The number 3. This number isn't just a number; it's the gold standard for anyone to catch recruiters' attention and really stand out in any job interview.

sentences.ar: لازم يكون في البرتفوليو بتاعه 3 مشاريع كاملة 3 مشاريع من البداية للنهاية
sentences.en: Their portfolio must have 3 complete projects, 3 projects from start to finish,

sentences.ar: بيغطوا كل التقنيات اللي تكلمنا عنها وبيثبتوا عمليا أن دي مش مجرد معرفة نظرية
sentences.en: covering all the technologies we talked about and proving in practice that this isn't just theoretical knowledge.

sentences.ar: لأ دي مشاريع تبنت بالإيد واشتغلت عمليا
sentences.en: No, these are projects built by hand that actually ran.

sentences.ar: وفي النهاية خلينا نفكر في السؤال المهم ده
sentences.en: And finally, let's think about this important question.

sentences.ar: هل الجيل الجاي من منصات البيانات هيتبني على إيد ناس بتكتفي بالفرجة والمشاهدة ولا ناس بتبني وتجرب بنفسها
sentences.en: Will the next generation of data platforms be built by people content with just watching, or by people who build and experiment themselves?

sentences.ar: الإجابة أكيد واضحة كفاية بقى فرجة على التوتوريال
sentences.en: The answer is surely clear: enough watching tutorials.

sentences.ar: وده الوقت المناسب لبداية بناء نسخة حقيقية من ShopFlow خطوة بخطوة من الصفر لحد الذكاء الاصطناعي
sentences.en: And this is the right time to start building a real version of ShopFlow, step by step, from zero all the way to AI.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.

first_mention_gloss.gloss_ar: إن تكرار نفس الطلب ما يعملش أثر زيادة
إن key واحد شايل أغلب الداتا

glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: An organized store of data managed by software that lets many users and programs safely read, write and query it.
concepts.failure: Treating a database as a bigger spreadsheet, ignoring keys, constraints and concurrent writes.

concepts.def_en: Data too large or fast to store or process on a single machine, so it is split and processed across a cluster.
concepts.failure: Calling any large file big data; if one machine can handle it, it is not.

concepts.def_en: A readable, general-purpose programming language widely used for data analysis, automation, pipelines and AI work.
concepts.failure: Using plain loops over huge data instead of vectorized pandas or SQL operations.

concepts.def_en: A message or failure signalling that something went wrong; read it first, since it usually names the cause and the location.
concepts.failure: Pasting the error into a search engine without first reading the terminal output.

concepts.def_en: Environment variable listing the folders the shell searches, in order, to find the program behind a typed command.
concepts.failure: Getting 'command not found' because the program's folder isn't listed in PATH.

concepts.def_en: Last-in, first-out structure; in memory, the call stack where function frames are pushed on call and popped on return.
concepts.failure: Mixing up stack and heap, or recursing too deeply until the stack overflows.

concepts.def_en: Two senses: the memory region where objects live beyond a call, and a priority queue yielding the smallest item first.
concepts.failure: Confusing stack and heap; objects live on the heap, frames hold references.

concepts.def_en: Structured Query Language: the standard declarative language for querying and changing data in relational databases by describing what you want.
concepts.failure: Thinking SQL runs in written order; the engine plans execution in its own order.

concepts.def_en: A widely used open-source relational database that stores data in tables and is queried with SQL.
concepts.failure: Assuming MySQL and PostgreSQL behave identically in SQL dialect and defaults.

concepts.def_en: Four guarantees for transactions: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability, so committed data stays correct and safe.
concepts.failure: Assuming ACID alone prevents every concurrency bug, whatever the isolation level.

concepts.def_en: Data organized into rows and columns under a fixed structure; the basic building block of a relational database.
concepts.failure: Treating a table like a spreadsheet: mixed meanings, merged cells and no keys.

concepts.def_en: Combines rows from two tables by matching key columns, such as orders with their customers.
concepts.failure: Joining on a non-unique key silently multiplies rows and inflates totals.

concepts.def_en: A command that shows the query plan the optimizer chose, with estimated and, in ANALYZE mode, actual rows and costs.
concepts.failure: Reading operator names but ignoring the gap between estimated and actual rows.

concepts.def_en: A request to a database or search system to fetch, filter or change data; in SQL, usually a SELECT statement.
concepts.failure: Blaming hardware for a slow query when a full table scan is the cause.

concepts.def_en: Reading rows by walking through pages: a full scan reads every page, while an index seek goes straight to the matches.
concepts.failure: A non-sargable filter forces a full scan that reads every page.

concepts.def_en: Uneven distribution where one key holds most of the data, so one partition's task runs far longer than the rest.
concepts.failure: Adding executors to fix it; the one hot key still lands on one task.

concepts.def_en: A graph whose edges have direction and no cycles, used to model task dependencies so work can be ordered and run.
concepts.failure: A dependency loop creates a cycle, so no valid run order exists.

concepts.def_en: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to model relationships such as roads, dependencies or calls between functions.
concepts.failure: Confusing a graph (nodes and edges) with a chart (plotted data).

concepts.def_en: A construct that repeats a block of code for each item or until a condition changes.
concepts.failure: Off-by-one bounds, or a condition that never changes, looping forever.

concepts.def_en: Apache Airflow: a platform that schedules and monitors workflows defined as DAGs of tasks, with retries, a calendar and a UI.
concepts.failure: Passing big data between tasks via XCom instead of storing it externally and passing references.

concepts.def_en: A chain of automated steps where each stage's output feeds the next, such as extract, transform and load for data.
concepts.failure: Not making steps idempotent, so a rerun duplicates or corrupts data.

concepts.def_en: Running an operation or request again gives the same result as running it once, so a stopped and rerun pipeline never duplicates data.
concepts.failure: Rerunning a plain INSERT load after failure and silently duplicating the data.

concepts.def_en: One unit of work in a DAG (an Airflow step or a Spark computation on one partition), run, retried and tracked individually.
concepts.failure: Making tasks non-idempotent, so a retry duplicates side effects such as double inserts.

concepts.def_en: Apache Spark: a distributed engine that processes large datasets in parallel across a cluster, keeping data in memory where possible.
concepts.failure: Using Spark for small data, where cluster overhead outweighs any speed gain.

concepts.def_en: A distributed, append-only event log: producers write events to topics, consumers read forward, and events are retained for a set window.
concepts.failure: Treating Kafka as a database with a different name; it is a log with retention.

concepts.def_en: Processing data continuously as events arrive, instead of waiting to process it in periodic batches.
concepts.failure: Assuming events arrive on time and in order; late data breaks results.

concepts.def_en: Hadoop Distributed File System: splits files into blocks spread across DataNodes and keeps several replicas of each on different machines.
concepts.failure: Storing huge numbers of tiny files, which overload the NameNode's metadata memory.

concepts.def_en: Keeping several copies of the same data on different machines, so a failure loses nothing and the cluster can re-create missing copies.
concepts.failure: Mistaking replication for backup; a bad delete or corruption copies to every replica.

concepts.def_en: Apache CarbonData: a columnar file format with a multi-level index for fast queries on big data in the Hadoop ecosystem.
concepts.failure: Using it for small data where a regular database is simpler.

concepts.def_en: A separate sorted lookup structure on one or more columns that lets a database find rows without scanning the whole table.
concepts.failure: Adding an index on every column; each one slows writes and may never be used.

concepts.def_en: A single screen of charts and key numbers that lets people monitor metrics and make decisions quickly from data.
concepts.failure: Cramming many unrelated charts together, so viewers cannot see what to act on.

concepts.def_en: A pipeline that retrieves relevant passages from your own data and gives them to a language model, so answers rest on real sources.
concepts.failure: Blaming the generator when most RAG failures start earlier, in retrieval or chunking.

concepts.def_en: Finding and returning the most relevant documents or chunks for a query, using keyword, vector or hybrid search, before the model generates an answer.
concepts.failure: Blaming the LLM for wrong answers when retrieval returned the wrong passages.

concepts.def_en: When a model produces a fluent, convincing answer that is factually wrong or unsupported by any source.
concepts.failure: Believing fluent, confident wording signals correctness; it says nothing about truth.

concepts.def_en: Application Programming Interface: a defined contract through which one program requests data or actions from another, often over HTTP using JSON.
concepts.failure: Changing a response field or meaning without versioning, breaking every client that depends on it.

concepts.def_en: A statically typed, object-oriented language that runs on the JVM; used for large backend systems, APIs and big-data tooling.
concepts.failure: Ignoring null handling, leading to NullPointerException at runtime.

concepts.def_en: Interfaces through which programs call each other to request data or actions, typically over HTTP with JSON.
concepts.failure: Calling an API without handling errors, timeouts or rate limits.

concepts.def_en: A tool that packages an app with everything it needs into a container, so it runs the same way on any machine.
concepts.failure: Expecting data inside a container to persist after the container is removed.

concepts.def_en: Continuous integration plus continuous delivery: automated build, test and release steps that take each change from commit to deployable software.
concepts.failure: Automating deployment without automated tests or gates, shipping bad changes faster.

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.
Up to 6 kinetic words on at most 2 lines, each word arriving on its own spoken word anchor.
A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.
A counter that rolls from the previous value to the target over the spoken number (preset count).
An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
A SQL query split into its logical execution stages, lit in execution order.
Rows narrowing through query stages (FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ...).
A request travelling hops (client, lb, service, cache, db, queue, external) with per-hop latency.
A status stamp on a target.
Doors by clearance level; a keycard opens some.
Deep-Dive entry card with parent chapter and prerequisite concepts.
